name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Use the latest Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet for EXCAVA’s core reasoning layer. It’s the strongest open model today, beating older versions by ~0.7% on complex tasks—enough to clear the 0.5% threshold. The trade-off is higher API costs, but we offset it by running only the critical inference path through Sonnet while keeping cheaper models for simpler steps.

name: Torque
text: Claude 3.7 Sonnet’s 0.7% gain is real but fragile—it’s benchmarked on narrow tasks, not EXCAVA’s messy, real-world inputs. The real risk isn’t cost; it’s that the model’s verbosity will bloat EXCAVA’s latency past the point where 0.5% gain becomes irrelevant. Test it live on a 1% traffic slice for 24 hours—if p95 latency rises more than 1%, we scrap it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run EXCAVA’s core reasoning on the latest Llama 3.4 405B Instruct. It’s the strongest open model today, beats older Llama by ~0.8% on complex tasks, and costs 30% less than Claude 3.7 Sonnet. The trade-off is higher latency—about 120ms more per call—but we keep it under 500ms by caching frequent queries.

name: Torque
text: Llama 3.4 405B’s 120ms latency hit is a real risk—EXCAVA’s real-time pipeline can’t absorb that without degrading user experience, and caching won’t save you if the model’s output length spikes unpredictably. Test it on a 1% slice, but only after measuring end-to-end latency under load; if it breaches 500ms, scrap it. Better alternative: run a 1-shot distilled variant of Llama 3.4 405B—faster, cheaper, and likely within the 0.5% gain if the distillation preserves core reasoning.
